note: Profile fit is close to textbook. Associate in banking with a master's in finance, working 12-14 hour days, health is plainly the neglected corner rather than a crisis, and he is the clearest good-to-great case in the batch — 5'10", 175 lb, roughly 15-18% body fat, an ex-competitive powerlifter chasing a one-arm pull-up and 30-minute EMOMs, who says outright that being ahead of the average is 'not good enough for me.' He fails only on income, and fails it in an instructive way: he is not price-sensitive at all — he called $6,000 fair, refused to ask for a discount, and said a $300-a-month price would have made him suspect the programme. The block is liquidity, not willingness, and it has a stated four-to-six month end date. This is the case the ICP observation about 'makes good money doing the work a payment plan already solves' points at, except here the prospect rejected the payment plan too.
